key_insight: Parametric subharmonic instability (PSI) can generate small-scale turbulence in ocean bottom boundary layers due to adjustments in wave frequency from baroclinic flows.
engineering_relevance: Understanding PSI may improve our ability to predict near-bottom mixing processes in marine environments.
method: Linear stability analysis of the bottom boundary layer.
Nonlinear simulations to assess the growth rate of PSI.
Evaluation of energy sources including wave shear and buoyancy production.
evidence_signal: PSI's growth rate is influenced by the vertical stratification of the bottom boundary layer and the slope Burger number.
watch_item: The increasing importance of geostrophic shear production as flows approach marginal stability may complicate predictions.
paper_title: Parametric Subharmonic Instability in the Ocean Bottom Boundary Layer
